text:
Sara: Quick sync — we need to converge on SDK surface for pagination+retries+resume across py/ts/go. I sketched 2 options:

Sara: Option A (cursor-first):

```
# python
for item in client.list_things(cursor=None):
    ...
```

Sara: Option B (iterator object):

```
# python
it = client.list_things_iter(page_size=100)
item = next(it)
it.pause_resume_token()  # return opaque token
```

Sara: Key goals: simple resume semantics for mobile/offline clients, clear idempotency for retry, minimal cross-lang surface mismatch.

Ben: +1 on explicit resume token. Iterator hides token too much for some customers. We should provide both but make the 'resume token' first-class.

Carla: Agree. For TS ergonomics we can return {items, nextCursor} on each page and provide async iterator helper (easy to import). For Go, idiomatic is channel or stream function; we'd probably expose both: Page(ctx, opts) and Stream(ctx, handler).

David: Python implementation note: current generator-based iterators can't be pickled reliably. If we want offline resume, we must return a serializable token alongside each page result. So API like `Page(items, resume_token)` seems safest.

Emily: TS draft:

```
// async iterator helper
for await (const item of client.pages('list', { pageSize: 100 })) {
  // item: {rows: Thing[], nextCursor?: string}
}
```

Emily: Also propose `retryOptions` per-call: `{retries: number, backoff: 'exp'|'const', idempotencyKey?: string}`

Ben: Transport question: should retry semantics live at transport layer (fetch/gRPC) or at SDK call layer? If we put them at transport, streaming resume becomes awkward.

Carla: My view: core retry for unary calls in transport; SDK layer implements page-level retries with awareness of resume tokens/idempotency. For streaming we offer best-effort resume helpers but document weaker guarantees.

Emily: We also need to standardize retryable status codes: e.g., 429, 502, 503, 504 + network errors. Add an opt-in for 'unsafe-retry' for non-idempotent ops.

David: Implementation risks: double-apply retries if both transport and sdk do them. Need a sentinel header or flag to disable transport-auto when SDK-managed retrying.

Sara: Good call. Proposal: transport exposes `autoRetry: boolean` default true for simple calls. SDK pagination sets `autoRetry:false` and uses its own `pageRetry` with resume token logic. Add `x-sdk-retry-coordinator: 1` header to opt-out.

infra-bot: deploy: infra note — adding header may affect proxies and caches; ensure header is whitelisted.

Ben: Another tradeoff: returning per-page tokens vs per-item tokens. Per-page simpler; per-item gives finer resume but more overhead. Recommend per-page for first pass.

Carla: UX: put helper `client.list_things.resume(token)` which returns iterator starting from token. That keeps surface minimal.

Emily: Will add TS typings and small helper lib to convert page-based responses into item-iterators.

David: For docs: clearly mark that resume tokens are opaque and only valid for N minutes/versions. Also add example for mobile offline sync.

Sara: Next steps: Carla to draft API sketches for py/ts/go, David/Emily to prototype token + serializer, Ben to check transport sentinel header flow with infra.

Sara: Thanks. Ping me in thread when you have PRs. :raised_hands:
